arithmetic_intensity_details.theoretical_assumptions: perfect reuse of the 3-row neighbourhood in cache: u read once (8 B), v written once (8 B) plus its write-allocate read (8 B)
arithmetic_intensity_details.as_implemented_note: NumPy evaluates the update in 4 passes through a temporary (add, add, add, scale), each streaming ~24 B per point when the block exceeds cache

machine.flops_per_cycle_source: AVX2: 2 FMA units x 4 doubles x 2 FLOPs

peak_memory_bandwidth_theoretical.source: WMI Win32_PhysicalMemory; estimate assumes one 64-bit channel per module, at most 2 (consumer dual channel). Override with --peak-bw-gbs.

memory_bandwidth_measured.kernel: STREAM Add c = a + b, 24 B per element

conclusion: The stencil performs 4 FLOPs per 24 bytes (AI = 0.167 FLOP/B; 0.042 FLOP/B as implemented in NumPy). The machine balance (ridge point) is 5.0 FLOP/B, about 30x higher, so the kernel is memory-bandwidth bound: attainable performance is capped near AI x bandwidth = 8.5 GFLOP/s, far below the 256 GFLOP/s compute peak. The strong-scaling working set (37.5 MiB) exceeds L3 (12.0 MiB), so every sweep streams from DRAM. Adding cores helps only until the shared memory bandwidth saturates, which also limits strong-scaling efficiency.
